justifications.functional_suitability: Scoring Engine and Ingestion Service address scoring (R-01), while Case Management & Admin UI covers review (R-02). ML Runtime Evaluator explicitly handles zero-downtime model reloading (R-03), though fraud rule management mechanisms are minimally described.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Ingestion Handler uses low-overhead gRPC/Protobuf, and ML Runtime Evaluator uses embedded runtimes with memory-mapped files to satisfy <50ms P99 latency. Asynchronous audit flushing to Amazon S3 prevents blocking 3,000 TPS payment evaluations.
justifications.compatibility: Edge Router & Validator adheres to OpenAPI/REST standards to interface with External Payment Gateway. gRPC/Protobuf enables efficient internal interoperability between API Gateway / Ingestion Service and Scoring Engine.
justifications.usability: Fraud Analysts are served by a dedicated Case Management & Admin UI with a Single Page Application (SPA) Frontend backed by a BFF Container, providing accessible case inspection and rule management workflows.
justifications.reliability: Telemetry & Circuit Breaker Manager and DLQs and Quarantine Queues handle operational failures. However, an explicit fallback or fail-open mechanism ensuring payments are not blocked longer than 1 minute (R-07) is missing.
justifications.security: Audit Log Storage Component enforces tamper-evident 7-year WORM storage via S3 Object Lock (R-06). However, concrete mechanisms for tokenization, encryption, and masking card data from analysts (R-05, PCI-DSS) are omitted.
justifications.maintainability: Containers maintain clear boundaries, and managed AWS services suit a three-engineer team. However, the component model is inconsistent (e.g., 'AWS ECS with Fargate' erroneously lists top-level containers as its components), obscuring internal modularity.
justifications.portability: The design fits the AWS eu-west-1 target using AWS ECS with Fargate and S3. Relying on proprietary AWS capabilities (Cognito, S3 Object Lock) reduces broader cloud portability but satisfies target environment constraints.

PERF-01.justification: Embedded ML models with memory-mapped files and gRPC communication between the Ingestion Service and Scoring Engine support sub-50ms latency. Asynchronous audit logging prevents blocking the critical path.
sensitivity_points: In-process embedded ML execution eliminates external network hops.
Asynchronous flushing of audit records prevents storage latency spikes.
tradeoffs: Memory footprint per container increases to maintain local model weights.

PERF-02.justification: Case management queries run via Aurora Serverless and a separate BFF container, cleanly decoupling analyst load from the stateless real-time scoring engine.
sensitivity_points: Separation of operational database queries from real-time scoring compute path.
tradeoffs: Eventual consistency between real-time decisions and case management records.

AVAIL-01.justification: Telemetry and circuit breakers are identified, but specific fallback scoring logic within the API Gateway to render fallback decisions and emit audit logs during scoring engine downtime is underspecified.
sensitivity_points: Fast failure detection and circuit tripping at the ingestion layer.
tradeoffs: Default approval during scoring failure risks fraud loss versus checkout abandonment.

AVAIL-02.justification: Audit records are batched and flushed asynchronously, with SQS standard and dead-letter queues available to absorb backpressure or failures if S3 is degraded.
sensitivity_points: Local memory and queue buffering capacity during downstream S3 latency spikes.
tradeoffs: Asynchronous buffering risks data loss on node termination unless backed by durable storage.

MOD-01.justification: The Scoring Engine explicitly incorporates zero-downtime model weight hot-reloading using memory-mapped files and records model versions alongside decision outputs.
sensitivity_points: Memory-mapped hot-reloading mechanism efficiency without restarting engine containers.
tradeoffs: Running multiple model versions in memory concurrently increases Fargate instance sizing.

MOD-02.justification: While UI rule administration is indicated, the runtime rule evaluation pipeline, dynamic rule distribution to scoring instances, and explanation generation components are missing from the container and component models.
sensitivity_points: Dynamic rule distribution propagation time across distributed scoring engines.
tradeoffs: Dynamic rule parsing adds evaluation latency compared to statically compiled rules.

SEC-01.justification: Cognito handles authentication and RBAC, but critical mechanisms for tokenization, PAN masking, and automated anomaly detection for compromised analyst accounts are entirely missing from the architecture.
sensitivity_points: Absence of a dedicated tokenization service or PAN masking layer in case views.
tradeoffs: Relying on basic CloudWatch metrics over specialized SIEM delays compromised credential detection.

SEC-02.justification: S3 with Object Lock in WORM compliance mode alongside Glacier Vault Lock ensures tamper-evident retention for 7 years, storing inputs, model versions, and audit logs.
sensitivity_points: Queryability and indexing of archived S3/Glacier records over long retention periods.
tradeoffs: Transitioning to Glacier Vault Lock reduces storage costs but increases retrieval times.
